note: Every answer this adapter can be given, and what each one means. Two of them carry the claims that matter. A repository with no open issue and a search that matched nothing are the origin saying there is nothing there, and neither is a payload that moved. And GitHub's documented answer to an anonymous client that has spent its hour is 403 with a message about rate limits — so a 403 here is never `auth_required`: waiting fixes it and a credential is not required to have the capability at all, which is the whole of criterion 1. The payload shapes are this package's belief; the 2026-08-10 probes record statuses and a ceiling, not bodies, and offline determinism forbids capturing one here.

cases.evidence: the roster row names issues; the collection is a path segment under the repository
the roster row names releases; the same route at a different collection
measured: api.github.com/search/repositories answered 200 anonymously, on the code_search bucket

cases.query: a phrase nobody has ever committed
cases.evidence: the index still answers with its container and a total of zero: nothing matched, and nothing moved
an empty list is a repository with nothing open, which is a fact about the repository rather than about this read
a row short of its declared fields says so on the record; a star count of zero is a count and not an omission
200 with an object naming neither `id` nor `full_name`: the payload this adapter reads has changed shape
200 with no `items` list: not a search that matched nothing
the origin's own status for a repository it will not show an anonymous client, carried as itself

GitHub answers an anonymous client that has spent its 60/hr with 403 and a message about rate limits. Waiting fixes it, so it is never `auth_required`: a keyless route reported as credentialed is the false capability this whole spec exists to prevent
